title: E.ON and OVO Takeover: What It Means for Customers
description: E.ON is buying OVO after competition clearance in October 2026. What happens to OVO tariffs, credit, direct debits and switching while the deal completes.
h1: E.ON and OVO takeover: what it means for you
intro: E.ON’s purchase of OVO has been cleared by the competition regulator. If you’re an OVO customer, here’s what changes, and what doesn’t.

image.alt: Transmission towers silhouetted under a green-tinted sky

cardText: Tariffs, credit and switching during the takeover.

sources.title: Which?: what the takeover means for OVO customers

sections.html: E.ON has agreed to buy OVO, and the deal received competition clearance in early October 2026. Reports put E.ON’s household customers at around 5.6 million and OVO’s at around 4 million, which would make the combined business one of Britain’s largest suppliers. Completion is expected later, with Which? suggesting by the end of the year.

• Nothing changes until the deal completes: same account, payments and contact details.
  • Your tariff, including any fix, is honoured until its end date.
  • Your supply won’t be interrupted.
  • You can still switch away if you find a better deal (check exit fees on fixes).
  • Take a meter reading and a screenshot of your balance, so you have a record of any credit or debt.
Only if there’s a better deal for you. Compare tariffs as usual using our deal checklist and see all UK suppliers.
